strategy.thesis: Hospital-backed 'VC × accelerator × hospital' model: Taiwan's largest medtech/healthtech accelerator partners directly with hospitals to give precision-medicine, medical-device and digital-health startups real clinical validation sites, cutting commercialization timelines from 7-8 years to 3-5 years and serving as a gateway into Asia.

summary.en: BE Health Ventures (比翼生醫, formerly BE Accelerator / BE Capital) is Taiwan's largest medtech and healthtech startup accelerator and a hospital-backed VC, founded around 2018. Using a 'VC × accelerator × hospital' model with partners including Taipei Medical University, Show Chwan and Kaohsiung Medical University, it has mentored 140+ biomedical startups and invested in roughly 30; its 25 invested portfolio companies have raised about US$200M in total. Its PoC clinical-validation program (5-6 months) guarantees a US$500K investment in one selected startup, and it is expanding into Japan.

summary.en: FinTechSpace (金融科技創新園區) is Taiwan's first fintech-focused co-working hub and accelerator, opened in September 2018 under the guidance of the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), planned by the Taiwan Financial Services Roundtable (TFSR) and executed by the Institute for Information Industry (III) — building on the earlier FintechBase. Its first residency wave admitted 37 teams from 64 applicants (31 domestic, 6 international), and it has supported 200+ fintech startups across payments, wealthtech, insurtech, regtech, blockchain, eKYC/eAML and AI, supported by a Digital Sandbox, Regulation Clinic and 100+ partner organizations.

summary.en: HAOSHi Accelerator (好食好事) is Taiwan's first and largest agri-food tech accelerator, founded in 2018 by the non-profit HAOSHi Foundation (established 2017 by the Ting Hsin Wei-Te Charity Fund). Its free ~4-month program (no equity; refundable NT$20,000 deposit) covers agri-food supply-chain tech, food biotech, alternative protein and precision nutrition. Since 2018 it has accelerated 78+ startups with 60-70+ mentors; alumni report cumulative revenue of US$1.8B+ and follow-on investment of US$108.8M+, with a 40%+ investment rate.

summary.en: Wistron Accelerator (緯創加速器) is a corporate vertical accelerator launched in 2021 by Taiwanese hardware giant Wistron, operated by AppWorks. It runs twice a year, recruits about 7 startups per batch in AI, IoT, cloud and cybersecurity (also edutech/medtech), and is equity-free and fee-free, instead giving NT$200,000 sponsorship and direct access to Wistron Group C-level mentors. Across its first eight batches it selected 40 startups and made 36 investments.

summary.en: MOX (Mobile Only Accelerator) was a Taipei-based, mobile-first/mobile-only accelerator run by US VC firm SOSV — the first international accelerator in Taiwan — targeting the 'next 4 billion' mobile-only consumers in India, Indonesia and the rest of Southeast Asia. summary.en: Smart Capital (識富天使會) is Taiwan's largest individual-angel community, founded in 2017 out of WorkFace Taipei. It reported 250+ members and ~40 startups (3 'funds', >NT$100M total) by 2021, growing to 500+ members and 50+ startups by 2025, with 94% of portfolio still active. summary.en: AVA Angels (安發天使投資 / 安致勤資) is a Taipei angel-investment platform founded around 2020 by JJ Fang (方俊傑) that blends angel co-investment with a VC-fund structure and weekly investor meetings. It reports US$18M AUM, 37 portfolio companies and 30+ investors, focusing on AI, SaaS, FinTech, consumer tech, Web3 and ESG. Funds include the 2021 'AVA Yuan' angel fund (>NT$100M) and the AVA Sustainable Fund; checks run US$300K–1M. FINDIT ranks it Taiwan's most active angel org in recent years. It also runs the A2Growth Launchpad accelerator.

summary.en: The Taiwan Angel Investment Association (台灣天使投資協會) is a non-profit founded on 29 March 2013 (Youth Day) to build a friendlier early-stage investment ecosystem in Taiwan. strategy.thesis: Taiwan's first government venture-capital mechanism embedded in environmental policy. The National Development Fund and Ministry of Environment co-invest with private capital across six net-zero domains — resource circulation, deep energy efficiency, forward-looking energy & energy storage, digital/low-carbon technology, carbon capture & negative-carbon technology, and climate-adaptation/disaster-prevention technology — to seed a domestic green-startup ecosystem over a 10-year horizon.

summary.en: A NT$10 billion (US$318M) government co-investment fund launched in 2024 by Taiwan's Ministry of Environment and National Development Fund — the country's first venture-capital mechanism built into environmental policy — channeling capital with private partners into six net-zero technology domains over 10 years.

funds.name: 生鵬一號基金 (Sheng Peng Fund No.1)

strategy.thesis: A NT$2 billion biotech venture fund established by Taiwan's government-affiliated Development Center for Biotechnology (DCB), backed by domestic private capital, the National Development Fund and Japanese/Singaporean investors, to invest in medical devices and new-drug startups and pull DCB-incubated 'Venture Studio' teams into international markets.

summary.en: Sheng Peng Fund No.1 (生鵬一號基金) is a NT$2 billion biotech venture fund set up by Taiwan's government-affiliated Development Center for Biotechnology (DCB). Announced in 2021 and targeted to launch in 2022, it was a landmark vehicle that broke a 20-year rule limiting government-founded foundations from investing, drawing on domestic private capital, the National Development Fund and Japanese/Singaporean LPs to fund medical-device and new-drug startups alongside DCB's incubation 'Venture Studio'.

strategy.thesis: A government agricultural-development-fund investment program run by Taiwan's Ministry of Agriculture (formerly Council of Agriculture). Capital is entrusted to trustee financial institutions which set up a VC review panel and co-invest equity in young agricultural-science R&D companies — covering new varieties, technologies, products and technical services across agriculture, forestry, fisheries and animal husbandry.

summary.en: The hardware-focused 'Buffalo' technology funds of Taiwania Capital (national-level VC founded 2017 with NDC, ITRI's ITIC and Bank of Taiwan). The first IoT fund raised NT$4.65bn (2017) and Buffalo V raised NT$1.5bn (~US$50M, 2021), investing in IoT, next-gen semiconductor, sensors, robots/drones and AI across Taiwan and the US.

summary.local: 位於多倫多的早期深科技創投（第三期基金3,000萬美元、59家投資組合），由Wattpad共同創辦人劉欣（Eva Lau）與劉允（Allen Lau）創立，專注軟硬整合深科技——半導體、神經型態系統、AI晶片與機器人，並明確善用台灣供應鏈與資金支持其投資組合。

Described by Standard Chartered as the first VC firm in Taiwan dedicated to supporting female entrepreneurs.

Operates as a social enterprise blending storytelling/media, resource matching and minority seed investments (capped at <=50% of investee capital) in women-founded ventures, recycling returns rather than distributing profit.
summary.local: 2012 年由張舒眉以個人積蓄成立的女力媒合社會企業，結合深度內容、資源媒合與對女性創業者的種子投資（投資上限為對方資本額 50%），所得回饋滾入基金繼續支持下一位女性創業家，被渣打銀行稱為台灣第一家專注支持女性創業家的創投。

sources.supports: Founding year, founder, social-enterprise structure, investment approach, portfolio examples

name.local: 社企流 iLab 育成計畫／加速器

strategy.thesis: Taiwan's first impact-focused startup accelerator, run by social-innovation media platform SEInsights (社企流). The growth-stage accelerator track (launched 2019) was co-created with B Current / Huoshuei impact investment (活水) — described as Taiwan's first incubation mechanism designed for growth-stage impact enterprises.

program.eligibility: Accelerator track: impact enterprises with annual revenue above NT$5,000,000 that can demonstrate measurable impact. Incubator track: early-stage social-innovation teams.

application.how_to_apply: Apply during open call windows announced on ilab.seinsights.asia and SEInsights channels.

summary.en: Launched in 2014 by social-innovation media SEInsights (社企流), iLab is Taiwan's first impact-focused incubation/acceleration program. Over six years it incubated 133 teams that collectively raised more than NT$100 million; its growth-stage accelerator track (2019) was co-created with B Current/Huoshuei (活水) impact investment.
summary.local: 社企流 iLab 育成計畫於 2014 年啟動，是全台第一個著重「社會影響力」的創業育成／加速器。六年間共支持 133 組團隊、合作團隊累計募資逾 1 億台幣；2019 年的加速器（成長期）由社企流與活水社企投資開發攜手創立，為全台第一個針對成長期影響力企業設計的育成機制。

name.local: AWE 臺灣女性創業學院

strategy.thesis: A U.S. State Department flagship women-entrepreneurship program localized in Taiwan since 2021 by the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) together with Taiwan's SME and Startup Administration (MOEA) and Meta. Delivers training, mentorship and (since 2023) an accelerator bootcamp focused on funding, market expansion and international engagement for women founders.

perks: International network access via AIT / U.S. State Department
program.eligibility: Women founders or aspiring founders in Taiwan, typically with English-communication ability for the international track.

application.how_to_apply: Annual open recruitment via AIT / SME Startup Administration; 2025 cohort applications ran through 30 April.

summary.en: AWE Taiwan is the local edition of the U.S. State Department's Academy for Women Entrepreneurs, run since 2021 by AIT with Taiwan's MOEA SME & Startup Administration and Meta. Over five-month cohorts it trains and mentors women founders (~240 alumnae, 37+ mentors); since 2023 it adds an accelerator bootcamp targeting funding, market expansion and international engagement.
summary.local: AWE 臺灣女性創業學院為美國國務院「女性創業學院」在台版本，自 2021 年起由美國在台協會（AIT）攜手經濟部中小及新創企業署與 Meta 共同辦理。五個月課程培訓並輔導女性創業者（累計近 240 位校友、37 位以上業師），2023 年起加入加速器訓練營，協助女性創業家取得資金、拓展市場並接軌國際。

strategy.thesis: Long-running national women-entrepreneurship program of Taiwan's MOEA SME & Startup Administration. Provides staged support to women founders: free training courses, a 6-month women's accelerator (funding + market expansion), the Women Entrepreneur Awards (女性創業菁英獎), the AWE Taiwan academy, and overseas-market assistance.

perks: Women Entrepreneur Awards (女性創業菁英獎)
program.eligibility: Women in Taiwan who are starting or running businesses; specific tracks for early-stage and growth-stage women founders.

application.how_to_apply: Apply per track via the program website and the contractor (產業競爭力發展中心 / sysme); the 15th Women Entrepreneur Awards and 2026 academy selection were open as of March 2026.

summary.en: The Women Entrepreneurship 'Flying Goose' Program, run by Taiwan's MOEA SME & Startup Administration, is a long-standing national initiative supporting women founders through free courses, a 6-month women's accelerator, the Women Entrepreneur Awards (15th edition by 2026), the AWE academy, and overseas-market support.

name.en: Power of Women New Female Force Startup Accelerator
name.local: 新女力創業加速器計畫

aka: 新住民女性創業加速器計畫

strategy.thesis: A women-empowerment startup accelerator run by the Foundation for Women's Rights Promotion and Development (婦女權益促進發展基金會, WRP). Targets economically disadvantaged Taiwanese women and new-immigrant (新住民) women, using a 'training -> consulting -> competition funding' model to strengthen economic self-sufficiency and empowerment.

investment.raw: competition-based grant funding to selected proposals (amount undisclosed)

perks: Business-plan pitch competition with funding (競賽資金補助)
program.eligibility: Domestic economically disadvantaged women and new-immigrant women in Taiwan with entrepreneurial potential.

application.how_to_apply: Apply via the Power of Women / WRP program calls; selected participants progress to the funded pitch competition.

summary.en: Run by the Foundation for Women's Rights Promotion and Development (WRP), this accelerator began in late 2017 as a new-immigrant women's accelerator and was renamed in 2020 to include all Taiwanese women. It uses a training -> consulting -> competition-funding model; a 2022 survey estimated ~80% of participants raised monthly income by ~NT$10,000, totaling ~NT$21.6 million over four years.
summary.local: 由財團法人婦女權益促進發展基金會辦理，2017 年底開辦（原為「新住民女性創業加速器」，2020 年納入本國女性並更名「新女力創業加速器」）。採「培力課程→諮詢輔導→競賽資金補助」模式，鎖定弱勢與新住民女性；依 111 年調查，約八成參與者每月平均增加約一萬元收入，四年累計約 2,160 萬元。

name.en: Standard Chartered Women in Entrepreneurship Award

strategy.thesis: A corporate-philanthropy women-founder award and acceleration program under Standard Chartered's Futuremakers initiative, delivered with the Garden of Hope Foundation (勵馨基金會) and Impact Hub Taipei. Provides seed/prize funding plus mentorship and bootcamp training to young women founders whose ventures show social impact in social inclusion, innovative technology, or environmental sustainability.

program.cohort_size: 10 selected enterprises per edition (3 winners + 7 finalists)

investment.raw: NT$2,000,000 total prize pool (3rd edition): NT$600,000 / NT$400,000 / NT$300,000 + NT$100,000 x7

application_cycles: Annual; 2026 (4th) edition applications ran 4 Mar - 20 Apr 2026

application.how_to_apply: Apply online via wiegoh.tw during the annual call with a submitted business plan.

summary.en: Launched in 2023 (4th edition in 2026), the Standard Chartered Women in Entrepreneurship Award is a corporate-philanthropy program (Futuremakers) delivered with the Garden of Hope Foundation and Impact Hub Taipei. It awards a total NT$2 million prize pool (NT$600K/400K/300K + NT$100K x7) plus mentorship and bootcamp training to young women founders building socially impactful ventures.
summary.local: 渣打女力創業獎自 2023 年首屆辦理（2026 年為第四屆），是渣打銀行 Futuremakers 公益計畫，與勵馨基金會及 Impact Hub Taipei 共同執行。提供總額新台幣 200 萬元獎金（首獎 60 萬、次獎 40 萬、三獎 30 萬，其餘 7 名各 10 萬）以及一對一業師輔導與訓練營，支持經營具社會影響力事業的年輕女性創業家。

investment.raw: Strategic investment and customer matching for top performers (amount undisclosed)

perks: Market validation fields and global channel resources
International supply-chain access (e.g. Walmart, McDonald's connections)
Strategic investment and customer matching for top teams
program.eligibility: Startups with complete implementation solutions / commercial readiness in ESG, green energy, smart manufacturing, smart cities, AI and net-zero retail.

application.how_to_apply: Apply via Taiwan Tech Arena (taiwanarena.tech) program call.

summary.en: ASPN Sports Tech Accelerator (originally launched in 2018-2019 as HYPE Global Virtual Accelerator Taiwan / SPIN Accelerator Taiwan) is Asia's first sports-technology accelerator. summary.en: Systex AGP (AI+ Generator Program / AI+新創加乘器計畫) is a non-profit, no-equity corporate accelerator run since 2018 by Taiwanese IT-services giant Systex. Unlike typical corporate accelerators it does not take equity or run generic fundraising/pitch training; instead it targets AI startups with validated, scalable products and connects them to Systex's ~40,000 enterprise clients for industry landing and global expansion. Over 7 years it has selected 52 startups; its 8th cohort (2025) picked 7 teams.

summary.en: The Taiwan Startup Institute (TSI / 產學研鏈結中心) is a national-level deep-tech accelerator established in 2017 under the Ministry of Science and Technology's 'Value Creation Program' (價創計畫) and headquartered at Taipei Tech. summary.en: The Koo Family Office manages the fortune of Taiwan's Koo dynasty — controlling shareholders of CTBC Financial Holding, KGI Financial, Taiwan Cement and Chailease — with a combined family wealth estimated at about US$7 billion. In November 2025, Andre Koo Sr. committed at least US$100M through the family office to anchor two new AI funds: US$50M into Era Funds (equity stakes in AI-infrastructure companies, e.g. Nvidia-ecosystem firms) and US$50M into a Chailease-managed private-credit fund, part of a US$1.5B AI raise. The next generation runs K8 Capital, a New York hybrid VC / private-credit firm targeting AI and enterprise-software startups.

strategy.thesis: Government co-investment scheme run by the National Development Fund alongside qualified angel investors, accelerators and VC firms, providing early-stage capital plus mentoring and networking to innovative Taiwanese startups; the NDF matches private angel capital rather than leading rounds.

summary.en: The NDF Business Angel Investment Program (創業天使投資方案) is a National Development Fund co-investment scheme launched in late 2018. The NDF invests alongside qualified angels, accelerators and VC firms in early Taiwanese startups (established <8 years, paid-in capital ≤NT$100M), investing up to NT$20M per case (first investment up to NT$30M, cumulative up to NT$100M). Originally budgeted at NT$1bn, it was scaled up to NT$10bn and runs until end-2030. As of 31 Aug 2022 it had backed 202 startups with NT$3.162bn of approved angel investment, crowding in NT$8.818bn of private capital.
summary.local: 行政院國家發展基金創業天使投資方案於 2018 年底推出,由國發基金與合格天使投資人、加速器及創投共同投資台灣早期新創(設立未逾 8 年、實收資本額或累計募資不超過新臺幣 1 億元),對同一事業投資以不超過 2,000 萬元為原則(初次最高 3,000 萬元、累計最高 1 億元)。初始預算 10 億元,後擴大為 100 億元,受理至民國 119 年(2030 年)底。截至 2022 年 8 月 31 日已投資 202 家新創,核定天使投資 31.62 億元,帶動民間投資 88.18 億元。

summary.en: SBIR (小型企業創新研發計畫) is a non-dilutive R&D grant program run by Taiwan's SME and Startup Administration (MOEA). It subsidises innovation by domestic SMEs across three phases: Phase 1 (prior research) up to NT$1.5M over 6 months; Phase 2 (R&D) up to NT$6M per year and NT$12M total over 2 years; and Phase 2+ (value-added application) up to NT$6M over up to 1 year. Eligible applicants are domestic SMEs with paid-in capital under NT$100M or fewer than 200 employees; applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

strategy.thesis: MOEA (Industrial Development Administration / former Department of Industrial Technology) matching R&D grant guiding enterprises to invest in forward-looking, cross-domain industrial technology development; subsidises forefront technology R&D, integrated R&D and the establishment of in-Taiwan R&D centres.

summary.en: The A+ Industrial Innovative R&D Program (A+企業創新研發淬鍊計畫) is a MOEA matching R&D grant launched in 2014 (then under the Department of Industrial Technology, now the Industrial Development Administration). It guides enterprises to invest in forward-looking, cross-domain industrial technology through three tracks — forefront technology R&D, integrated R&D, and establishing R&D centres in Taiwan. The subsidy covers in principle 40% and up to a maximum 50% of total project cost, with the remainder self-funded. Eligible applicants are domestic, legally-registered, financially-sound, non-Chinese-invested businesses.

summary.en: Startup Island TAIWAN is the national startup brand jointly created by the National Development Council (NDC) and Taiwan's startup communities, launched and branded around 2020–2021 to raise the global visibility of Taiwanese startups (the badge/logo is free for any local startup to use). Its flagship 'NEXT BIG' program, launched in 2021 with nine startups (a further 13 added in 2023, 22 total), identifies benchmark startups — such as AmazingTalker and Hahow — and supports them with branding, overseas business development and international investment connections rather than direct funding.

strategy.thesis: Taiwan's first university-affiliated startup accelerator, founded at National Chiao Tung University (now NYCU). Empowers early-stage, growth-driven tech and lab-spinout startups through mentorship, investment support, co-working space, corporate innovation and global market-entry programs (incl. an Access-to-Taiwan / A2T landing program). Runs programs such as TTA, SPIN, iCAN and TX Venture.

summary.en: IAPS (陽明交大產業加速器), founded in 2013 at National Chiao Tung University (now NYCU) in Hsinchu, was the first university-affiliated startup accelerator established by academia in Taiwan. It has worked with 950+ startups and lab teams, with annual cumulative fundraising exceeding NT$300M (~US$10–11M per cohort). In 2015 it was ranked the top accelerator in the Asia-Pacific region and 7th globally by UBI Global. Programs include TTA, SPIN, iCAN and TX Venture, plus an Access-to-Taiwan (A2T) landing program for international startups.

summary.en: The TMU BioMed Accelerator (北醫生醫加速器), established by Taipei Medical University in 2018, is Taiwan's first international-class medical-university accelerator. It focuses on biomedical startups across digital health, AI and medical devices, running two cohorts a year and leveraging its 1-university/6–7-hospital clinical system (4,000+ beds, 7,000+ medical professionals). It has accelerated 100+ domestic and international startups and invested in around 8, co-investing with partner Wing Capital (比翼資本) — including US$100,000 each into three more mature teams. Teams have come from France, Singapore, Taiwan, Japan and Canada.

strategy.thesis: Taipei-based crypto quantitative-trading and market-making firm that has acted as a company builder in Web3 — most notably incubating WOO Network (Wootrade) and its WOO X (CEX) and WOOFi (DEX) products. Its venture arm Kronos Ventures was spun off into independent investment firm Proxima in 2026.

summary.en: Kronos Research is a Taiwan-founded (2018) crypto quantitative-trading and market-making firm that has also functioned as a Web3 company builder, incubating WOO Network (originally Wootrade) in 2019 and its WOO X / WOOFi exchanges. Its dedicated venture arm, Kronos Ventures, was transitioned into an independent investment firm, Proxima, in 2026. Included here for its in-house incubation activity, though its primary business is trading.
